# Planner — Progress Memory

> **This file is the agent's persistent memory.** The `Planner` agent
> (`.github/agents/planner.agent.md`) MUST read this at session start and update it at session
> end. Keep it accurate and current. Commit it together with the work it describes.

## Mission

Turn each changelog feature (from the Changelog Researcher's backlog) into a concrete,
step-by-step implementation plan for the `llm` VS Code extension. The planner does NOT write
code — only the Coder writes code.

## Active plan — 1.100-16 · MCP config generation uses `inputs` for secrets

- **Status:** Planned (2026-10-23)
- **Changelog:** VS Code 1.100 (Apr 2025) — AI-assisted MCP server configs generated by `MCP: Add Server` now generate `inputs` (variable references) for secrets instead of inlining them. No screenshots — no UI-fidelity requirement.
- **Grounding notes:** `src/extension.ts` — `llm.mcp.addServer` handler (line 365): name prompt → transport quick-pick; stdio path (line ~425–446) writes `{ command, args? }` with **no env support at all** (the gap); HTTP path writes `{ url }`. `src/mcp.ts` — `McpServerConfig` (line ~19) has `command/args/env/url`; `parseMcpServers` (line ~66) validates/coerces `args`/`env` but has no `inputs` handling; `McpClient` constructor (line ~277) spawns with `env: { ...process.env, ...(config.env ?? {}) }`. `src/mcpManager.ts` — `McpManager.setServers` (line 69) stores the parsed map; `ensureStarted` (line ~85) constructs `new McpClient(cfg)` / `new McpHttpClient(cfg)`; no inputs plumbing. `src/config.ts` line 91 — `mcpServers: parseMcpServers(c.get("mcp.servers", {}))` (unchanged; `inputs` flows through the same parse). `src/secrets.ts` — `scanForSecrets` is a text-scanner for diffs; **not reusable** for env-var-name detection (different shape); the extension has **no `SecretStorage`** usage anywhere (API key is a plain `llm.apiKey` setting), so in-memory session storage is the consistent choice. Smoke test: `mcp-s1` parseMcpServers block at line ~2726; hard gate `assertCount !== 766` at line 6285.
- **Spec (minimal, engine-agnostic):** (1) Config shape: a server entry may carry `inputs: { [name]: { description?, type?: "string"|"number"|"boolean", password?, required? } }` (MCP spec convention; `name` is the map key); `env` values may be `${input:name}` references. (2) `parseMcpServers` coerces `inputs` (plain-object entries with optional string `description`, `type` restricted to the three literals, boolean `password`/`required`); malformed `inputs` → left undefined (entry still kept). (3) Pure helpers in `src/mcp.ts`: `detectSecretEnvName(name)` — case-insensitive match on `key|token|secret|password|passwd|pwd|apikey|api_key|auth|credential|bearer`; `resolveMcpInputs(cfg, provided)` — substitutes `${input:name}` in `env` values from `provided` (exact-key lookup), throws `Error("missing required input: <name>")` when a referenced input is absent from `provided` (covers both `required: true` and plain absence — the server cannot start without it). (4) Prompting happens in the **extension host** (`src/extension.ts`): after the stdio `addServer` flow, prompt for env vars; secret-looking names are stored as `${input:...}` references + an `inputs` entry (`password: true`), and the user is immediately prompted for the values via `showInputBox({ password: true })`; resolved values are handed to the manager via a new `setInputs(name, values)` and kept in memory for the session (no SecretStorage — matches the existing plain-setting architecture).
- **Files to touch:** `src/mcp.ts`, `src/mcpManager.ts`, `src/extension.ts`, `package.json`, `scripts/smoke-test.js`.
- **Slices (in order):**
  - `1.100-16.S1` — `src/mcp.ts` only: (a) `export interface McpInput { description?: string; type?: "string" | "number" | "boolean"; password?: boolean; required?: boolean; }`; add `inputs?: Record<string, McpInput>` to `McpServerConfig`; (b) `parseMcpServers`: when `entry.inputs` is a plain object, coerce each entry — keep only entries whose `description` (if present) is a string, `type` (if present) is one of the three literals, `password`/`required` (if present) are booleans; if any entry fails, drop the whole `inputs` map (leave undefined) but keep the server entry; (c) `export function detectSecretEnvName(name: string): boolean` — `/key|token|secret|password|passwd|pwd|apikey|api_key|auth|credential|bearer/i` test; (d) `export function resolveMcpInputs(cfg: McpServerConfig, provided: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string>` — for each `env` value matching `/^\$\{input:([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\}$/`, look up the name in `provided`; missing → `throw new Error(\`missing required input: ${name}\`)`; non-reference values pass through; returns the resolved env map (empty object when `cfg.env` is undefined).
  - `1.100-16.S2` — `src/mcp.ts` + `src/mcpManager.ts`: (a) `McpClient` constructor takes an optional 2nd arg `inputs?: Record<string, string>`; before spawn, if `inputs` is non-empty, compute `const env = resolveMcpInputs(config, inputs)` and spawn with `env: { ...process.env, ...env }` (when `inputs` is empty/absent, behavior is byte-identical to today); (b) `McpManager`: add `private inputs = new Map<string, Record<string, string>>()`; `setInputs(name: string, values: Record<string, string>): void` stores (and clears on empty object); `setServers` drops `inputs` entries for removed servers; `ensureStarted` passes `this.inputs.get(name)` into `new McpClient(cfg, ...)` (HTTP path unchanged — `McpHttpClient` ignores inputs); wrap the client construction so a `resolveMcpInputs` throw is caught and surfaces as the existing `error` status + `notify` (message: `MCP server '<name>' failed to start: missing required input: X`).
  - `1.100-16.S3` — `src/extension.ts` + `package.json`: (a) `llm.mcp.addServer` stdio branch: after the args prompt, add an env prompt — `showInputBox({ prompt: "Environment variables (KEY=VALUE, comma-separated, optional)", placeHolder: "e.g. API_KEY=sk-..., PORT=8080" })`; parse `KEY=VALUE` pairs (split on first `=`, trim, skip malformed); for each pair: if `detectSecretEnvName(key)` → `env[key] = \`${input:${key}}\`` and `inputs[key] = { description: \`Value for ${key}\`, type: "string", password: true, required: true }`, else `env[key] = value`; write `servers[name] = { command, args?, env?, inputs? }` (omit empty `env`/`inputs`); (b) after the `cfg.update`, if any secret inputs were generated: for each, `showInputBox({ prompt: \`Enter value for ${key} (stored in memory for this session)\`, password: true })` (skip on cancel → leave unresolved; the server will fail to start with the descriptive error); collect the provided values and call `mcpManager.setInputs(name, values)` (guard: `mcpManager` may be undefined pre-activation — in that case show a warning that values must be re-entered after reload); (c) `package.json` — `llm.mcp.servers` description becomes: `"MCP servers to connect to. Each entry: { command, args?, env?, inputs? } (stdio) or { url } (Streamable HTTP / SSE). env values may reference inputs as \${input:name}; secret values are prompted at connect time."`
  - `1.100-16.S4` — `scripts/smoke-test.js` only (smoke guards, last): new `mcp-inputs-s1..s4` block before the hard gate: (a) `parseMcpServers` accepts a valid `inputs` map (`{ API_KEY: { type: "string", password: true, required: true } }`) and keeps `env: { API_KEY: "${input:API_KEY}" }` verbatim; (b) `parseMcpServers` drops `inputs` with a bad `type` (e.g. `"text"`) while keeping the server entry; (c) `detectSecretEnvName`: true for `API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `db_password`, `AUTH_HEADER`, `client_secret`, `Bearer`; false for `PORT`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `HOME`; (d) `resolveMcpInputs`: resolves `${input:API_KEY}` from a provided map, passes through non-reference values, and throws `missing required input: X` for an absent reference; (e) `McpManager.setInputs` + `ensureStarted` with a stdio server whose `env` is `{ API_KEY: "${input:API_KEY}" }`: without `setInputs` the start fails with an error status containing `missing required input: API_KEY`; with `setInputs` called first, the start proceeds (use the existing fast-failing binary pattern from the `mcp-s1` failure case); (f) static: `src/extension.ts` references `detectSecretEnvName` and `setInputs`; `package.json` `llm.mcp.servers` description mentions `inputs`; (g) raise the hard total-count gate **766 → 774** (8 new assertions).
- **First slice:** `1.100-16.S1`.
- **Acceptance:** compile + smoke pass (774); `llm.mcp.addServer` (stdio) with env vars where a name looks like a secret writes `inputs` + `${input:...}` references to `llm.mcp.servers` (no secret value ever lands in the setting); the user is prompted with a password input box and the value is held in memory for the session; a server with unresolved required inputs fails to start with a descriptive `missing required input: <name>` error surfaced via the existing status/notify path; non-secret env values are inlined as before; servers without `inputs` behave byte-identical to before (spawn env, parse, manager).
- **Open questions:** (1) Secret values are **session-only** (in-memory `Map` in `McpManager`) — no `SecretStorage`/persistence; consistent with the extension's existing plain-setting API-key architecture, but values must be re-entered after a window reload (documented in the prompt text); (2) `${input:...}` references are supported in `env` values only (the only place a secret can appear for stdio; HTTP `url` is out of scope); (3) the env prompt is a single comma-separated `KEY=VALUE` input box (no multi-line editor) — matches the existing single-line prompt style of the flow; (4) `McpHttpClient` ignores `inputs` entirely (no env for HTTP servers in the current config shape).
